transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, I'm the pre-visit assistant for your clinic. Before the appointment with Dr. Eval on Sunday 11 October at 02:08, I'd like to ask some questions about your health so your doctor is prepared. This conversation is recorded and shared with your doctor. I'm an automated assistant, not a doctor, so I can't tell you what's wrong. If at any point you feel very unwell, please call 911. Are you happy to continue?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that's fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. First, please tell me the patient's full name and date of birth. If you're answering for someone else, please also tell me how you're related to them.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Meera Shah, 10 August 1992.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. What's been troubling you? Please tell me about each problem and when it started.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes. I've had a fever for about three days now, and a cough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I’m sorry you’re feeling unwell. Have you been coughing up any phlegm, and have you had any shortness of breath or chest pain?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No phlegm, it's dry. And no, I haven't had any shortness of breath or chest pain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. What’s the highest temperature you’ve measured, and was it with a thermometer or just by feel?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: 102 last night. I have a thermometer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Is the fever there all the time or does it come and go? Any chills or shaking?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It comes and goes. Worst at night. Chills, yes. Not shaking badly, no.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Any sore throat, runny nose, ear pain, rash, headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of those.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Any burning when you pass urine, needing to go more often, back or side pain, or tummy pain, vomiting, or diarrhoea?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of those. My bowels and bladder are normal.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any body aches or joint pains, and have you been around anyone sick, or travelled recently?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I've had body aches since yesterday, all over, mostly in my legs. I haven't travelled anywhere, but a colleague had something similar last week.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. What do you do for work, and who do you live with? Also, are you pregnant or could you be pregnant, and when was the first day of your last period?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm a primary school teacher, and I live in the city with my husband. I'm not pregnant, and my period was about two weeks ago, regular.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any long-term health problems, any previous similar illness, or any hospital stays or operations?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of those. Just normal colds before.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you take any regular medicines, or have you taken anything for this fever and cough? Also, do you have any allergies to medicines or foods, and what happens if you take them?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I don't take any regular medicines. I did take paracetamol twice yesterday, and it brought the fever down for a few hours. I don't have any allergies that I know of.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Does anyone in your family have any major health problems? And do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use any other substances?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My father has type 2 diabetes. My mother is well, and I have one brother who's well. I've never smoked, and I have a glass of wine at weekends.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. A couple last questions: has your appetite or sleep changed, and are you able to drink fluids normally?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My appetite's been down, and I'm sleeping poorly because of the fever. I am able to drink fluids normally.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been on any steroids, chemotherapy, or other treatment that weakens your immune system?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Here are the main points: Fever for about 3 days, Dry cough for about 3 days, Body aches, all over, mostly in legs for since yesterday. Fever for about 3 days. Cough present with this illness. Cough is dry; no phlegm. Is that right, or is there anything you'd like to correct or add?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that's right.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's everything I need. Your doctor will see this before your appointment. Until your appointment, here is what you can do. Check your temperature every 2 hours while you are awake and record each reading on your patient page. Drink plenty of fluids such as water, oral rehydration solution or soups. Pale yellow urine is a good sign you are drinking enough. Rest as much as you can. Wear light clothing and keep the room comfortably cool. Avoid heavy blankets while you feel hot. Note any new symptoms and the time they started, so you can tell your doctor. Stay home from work or school and wash your hands often to avoid passing the illness on. Eat light, easy-to-digest food if you have an appetite. Please go to the emergency department or call 911 straight away if there is difficulty breathing or breathing very fast; new confusion, or being very drowsy or hard to wake; a stiff neck; a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it; being unable to keep any fluids down; a baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or more. You'll find this advice on your patient page too, where you can also log your readings. Is there anything else you'd like your doctor to know?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, I've added that for your doctor. You can end the call whenever you're ready.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's everything. Thank you.
